errors.text_span: “Custom Characters.” The outer ring, colored in light blue, is divided into six slices representing different types of virtual characters: “Comic Characters,” “Movie Characters,” “Teleplay Characters,” “Novel Characters,” “Game Characters,” and “Custom Characters.”
errors.evidence: The 'Custom Characters' slice is red, not light blue, and is not part of the outer ring of 'Virtual Characters'. It is a separate main group in the inner circle.

errors.text_span: This donut-style pie chart visually compares the distribution of character types across two main categories: “Virtual Characters” and “Real Characters.”
errors.evidence: The chart has three main categories, not two. The description omits 'Custom Characters' as a main group.

errors.text_span: The inner circle, also light blue, is labeled “Virtual Characters” and appears to represent the combined total of the outer ring segments.
errors.evidence: The inner circle is not entirely light blue; it contains three distinct colors (blue, red, green) for the three main groups. The description incorrectly implies the inner circle is monochromatic.
The description does not mention that the chart lacks a legend and percentage labels inside the slices.
The description does not mention that there is no visual emphasis such as exploding or offsetting of any slice.
The description incorrectly states that segments are arranged in clockwise descending order by size, but the atom checklist indicates no specific visual ordering based on size.

errors.text_span: The chart includes a legend that maps the colors to their respective categories,
errors.evidence: The chart does not include a legend, as explicitly stated in the atom checklist.

errors.text_span: while the exact percentages are not labeled, the relative sizes of the segments suggest that “Comic Characters” and “Game Characters” are the largest among the virtual categories, while “Custom Characters” is the smallest.
errors.evidence: The description infers relative sizes without explicit visual confirmation, which is an over-generalization. The atom checklist does not support this claim.
